checks.note: DD-API-KEY/DD-APPLICATION-KEY confirmed on the API page. Scoped application keys confirmed on the api-app-keys page. OAuth2 auth code + PKCE confirmed for partner integrations, with the client created in a Partner Sandbox Account. The PAT doc states that PATs can be sent as 'Authorization: Bearer' on REST calls (example GET /api/v2/users, no API key needed). So the record's doubt about Bearer on the REST API is resolved: it works, and SATs use the same header. The record's evidence URL for bearer was missing.

The pricing page confirms a Free tier (Infrastructure Monitoring, 5 Basic hosts, 1-day retention) and 'Start Free Trial' buttons. It does not state the trial length, no-card terms, or whether Free tier accounts get API/app keys. 'paid_plan' is not supported, because a self-serve trial exists. Closest supported value: self_serve_trial.

The API page describes an HTTP REST API returning JSON, with v1 and v2 endpoint groups. The 'broad' rating is a judgment: it is consistent with the many resource groups, but I did not count them. The page does not mention GraphQL.

The Datadog-hosted MCP setup docs list https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp for US1, with per-site endpoints for US3, US5, EU1, AP1, AP2 and UK1. They list OAuth 2.0, PAT/SAT bearer and API+app key auth. US1-FED and US2-FED are unsupported. The docs do not state overall GA vs Preview status and say the server is 'under significant development'.

ready_with_caveats is reasonable: REST, scoped keys, bearer tokens and an official MCP server all exist. The caveats are an org requirement, per-site endpoints, and unscoped keys inheriting full user permissions (confirmed). Rate limits are not stated on the pages fetched, so that remains unverified. The Free-tier API access caveat is unresolved.

corrected.one_liner: Cloud observability and security platform for infrastructure metrics, logs, APM traces, monitors, dashboards, and incidents.
corrected.auth_notes: REST API: API key in DD-API-KEY header, plus an application key in DD-APPLICATION-KEY for endpoints that read data or manage resources. Application keys can be scoped (user- or service-account-owned); unscoped keys get all of the creator's permissions. Personal access tokens and service access tokens can be sent as 'Authorization: Bearer' on REST calls with no API key (documented example: GET /api/v2/users; scopes and expiry apply; some calls such as creating application keys return 403). OAuth2 (authorization code with PKCE) is documented for partner integrations, with the client created in a Partner Sandbox Account. The same OAuth 2.0 and PAT/SAT methods work with the MCP server.
corrected.access_notes: Keys are created in any org by users with the right permissions. The pricing page confirms a Free tier (Infrastructure Monitoring, up to 5 Basic hosts, 1-day retention) and a self-serve free trial. Trial length, card requirement and whether the Free tier includes API/app key access were not confirmed on fetched pages. Third-party OAuth requires a Partner Sandbox Account.
corrected.blocker: Users need a Datadog org (trial or paid; Free tier is limited to Infra Monitoring, 5 hosts, and API access on it is unconfirmed). Per-site regional endpoints are required, and the MCP server does not support US1-FED/US2-FED. Third-party OAuth is tied to the partner sandbox/integration program. Rate limits were not confirmed. Unscoped application keys inherit the creator's full permissions.
